$comment: What this application declares about its own artifact benchmarks, read by
tools/benchmark/declaration.mjs. Opt-in: before this file existed the harness built
no artifact workloads at all, so `delivery/artifact-size` had no producer and the one
absolute limit in budgets.json - chainDepth 3 - was unreachable. ADR-0082.
backend points at the module the browser suite installs, not a second stub. The
harness imports it into Node and answers /auth and /api behind the static origin with
it, so a delivery number cannot drift from what the suite asserts, and it needs no
lazyRoutes are routes reached through a literal dynamic import, one workload each:
each sample opens the application signed in on /login - where every application chunk
is still cold - and navigates once. Four rather than all twenty: the question is how
many round trips a first navigation costs, and these four are the shapes that differ.
A leaf list, a leaf with a parent layout and a URL parameter, a form-heavy screen, and
a screen behind a scope guard.
staleReleaseRoute is deliberately none of them. It must still be uncached after the
release switch the workload simulates, which is only true of a route no other workload
